convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom for BlauTVI custom indicator and depends on two external .mqh libraries (SmoothAlgorithms.mqh, TradeAlgorithms.mqh) for core smoothing and trade execution logic

derived_values.name: TimeShiftSec - timeframe period in seconds for signal time calculation
min_rates_total - minimum bars required before indicator is ready

other_exits: BuyPosClose and SellPosClose input flags allow disabling signal-based closes independently of open signals

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MMMode=LOT means fixed lots (negative MM interpreted as lot size), MMMode=LOT means MM value as lot size; other MarginMode values would interpret MM as fraction of margin/deposit

custom_logic_notes: Signal logic uses 3-buffer comparison of BlauTVI indicator: Value[0]=bar SignalBar, Value[1]=bar SignalBar+1, Value[2]=bar SignalBar+2. Long condition: indicator was declining (Value[1]<Value[2]) and now rising (Value[0]>Value[1]) — trough reversal. Short condition: indicator was rising (Value[1]>Value[2]) and now declining (Value[0]<Value[1]) — peak reversal. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose are input toggles allowing independent enable/disable of each signal direction and close action. TradeAlgorithms.mqh handles all position open/close with internal position checks. Recount flag ensures signal recalculation on data availability issues.
python_conversion_notes: BlauTVI is a custom indicator (Tick Volume Index by William Blau) that requires SmoothAlgorithms.mqh for its triple-smoothing logic (XLength1, XLength2, XLength3). This must be reimplemented in Python — the indicator applies configurable smoothing (EMA/JJMA/VIDyA/AMA per XMA_Method) three times to tick-volume-derived data. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose with internal position checking, lot sizing (MarginMode enum), SL/TP in points, and deviation handling — must reimplement these wrappers. SL/TP values (1000/2000) are in points, need digit-adjustment awareness for 5-digit brokers. Signal logic is bar-based (SignalBar=1 means using previous completed bar), new-bar guard via CIsNewBar class. The SignalBar=0 special case bypasses new-bar check and processes every tick.
